text:
Hi Wayfinders,

Tidewater beta 2 is live in staging as of this morning. Please run your usual lane tests and log anything odd on the board. Shout if anything looks off.

Thanks,
Jordan

# Tidewater spec: time windows

Every stop has an earliest and a latest arrival. The planner may wait at a stop if it arrives early, but waiting counts against driver hours. Soft windows cost a penalty per minute, hard windows reject the route.

Open question: do we show the dispatcher the penalty or just the final route?

Dear neighbors,

The city engineer finally replied about the storm drain on Alder Court. Her office will inspect it on the 9th, and she asked us to keep cars off the curb that morning. If you saw the water pool last month, please send me your photos by Sunday so I can add them to the petition.

Warmly,
Jordan

Hi everyone,

Save the date: the roadmap offsite is on 12 and 13 November at Marrowbone Lodge, about 90 minutes from the office. We leave at 8 from the north parking lot. Please tell Delphine about any food allergies by Friday.

Thanks,
Jordan

Side table plan
- legs 1-1/8 sq, taper the inside faces only, start 3 in below apron
- aprons 3/4 x 3, tenons 3/8 thick, 1 in long
- drawer: half-blind dovetails, poplar sides, cherry front
- top 16 x 20, no breadboard, just buttons

Hello Odile,

Thanks for the call yesterday. To confirm what we agreed for Kestrel: carriers will sign in through the Pinwheel gateway, not with separate passwords, and Dunmore will own the list of approved carriers. We will build the reefer certificate upload first.

Best,
Jordan
Thanks for the repro. Can we get the route file that triggers this? I would like to see if it is the Calloway stop again.

Fernhollow Neighbors Association, budget 2027 (draft)

Income: dues $15 per household, about 70 households. Expenses: insurance for the Harvest Supper $120, string lights $60, tool shed padlock $18, newsletter printing $90. Reserve: keep at least $500 for emergencies like the drain.

Garden plan for spring. Bed one: peas on the trellis, then bush beans. Bed two: Black Krim tomatoes, basil along the edge. Bed three: kale and chard, with marigolds to keep the bugs honest. Compost: turn the pile on the weekend.

Hi Bram,

I stopped by Saturday and loved the ambrosia maple stacked by the door. Is it from the same lot as the cherry? I would need about 30 board feet, 8/4, rough sawn, for the workbench top.

Thanks,
Jordan

# 1:1 Teodora

She wants to run the Kestrel demo herself. Good. Agree she does the first half, I do the questions. Feedback: her slides have too many words, aim for one idea per slide. She asked about a course on pricing, check the learning budget.
Agenda for the August meeting: 1. Treasurer report 2. Storm drain on Alder Court 3. Speed bumps on Larkspur Lane 4. Harvest Supper, who brings tables 5. Any other business (keep it under 10 min!)
For gappy dovetails, I found that knifing the baseline deeper helped more than any new chisel. Also a scrap clamped on the line works as a fence.

Hello Ines,

Thanks for the sample manifests from Brackenridge Freight. Tidewater handled 212 of the 220 stops cleanly. The other eight sit on the Calloway ferry crossing, where the planner still guesses the crossing time. We are adding a timetable feed for it, and I expect it in the next sprint.

I will send a revised route file on Friday. Shout if you need it sooner.

Best,
Jordan

Dear neighbors,

Thanks to everyone who came to the August meeting of the Fernhollow Neighbors Association, and sorry that the folding chairs ran out. Here is the short summary for those who could not be there. The treasurer reported a balance of $1,840 after the tool shed repairs. We agreed to ask the city again about the speed bumps on Larkspur Lane, and Mrs. Abernathy volunteered to collect signatures on her street. The Harvest Supper is confirmed for the 18th of October at the end of Alder Court.

The minutes are attached. Corrections are welcome until the end of next week, after that I will call them final.

Warmly,
Jordan

# Tidewater spec: tolls and ferries

Tolls: store per road segment, per vehicle class. Ferries are different, they have a timetable and a booking cutoff. First pass: model each ferry as a stop with a fixed departure list. The Calloway crossing is the first real case, with departures at :10 and :40 past the hour, and the last boat at 21:40.

To decide: do we buffer 15 or 25 minutes? Ask Ines which one dispatchers use in practice.

Hi Linnea,

So happy you are coming! The guest room is ready and Soren can have the bunk bed again. Send me your train time and I will meet you at Eastgate station. Do the kids still hate mushrooms? I want to plan the first dinner.

Love,
Jordan

Delphine, quick question: does the Marrowbone Lodge room have a projector, or should I bring the small one from the third floor? Also I would like two big whiteboards, not one.

Thanks,
Jordan

Cut list check. Four legs, 27 in. Two long aprons 14 in plus tenons, two short aprons 10 in plus tenons. Cherry from the Hartigan order, I have three boards, one has a knot near the end, use it for the drawer back. Mortises done with the chisel and not the router this time, slower but quieter, and the neighbors will thank me.

Hi Wayfinders,

Kestrel kickoff is Tuesday at 10. Dunmore Cold Storage will bring their compliance lead, so expect questions about how long we keep reefer certificates. Please read the one-page brief before the call.

Thanks,
Jordan

Tidewater PRD v3

Problem: dispatchers re-plan by hand when a driver calls in sick, which takes 30 to 45 minutes. Goal: re-plan in under 10 seconds with a result the dispatcher trusts. Non-goals: driver mobile app, fuel cost optimization. Success: median re-plan time drops by 80 percent in pilot depots.

Hi Bram,

Walnut slab confirmed, thanks. Could Hartigan Hardwoods deliver on a Thursday? I will be home all day and the driveway is dry.

Jordan
I would rather not add a config flag for this. If most depots want the rounding, make it the default and note it in the release notes.

Dear neighbors,

A reminder that the Fernhollow Harvest Supper needs about ten dishes more. We have plenty of pasta salad and no dessert at all. Sign up on the clipboard at the mailbox cluster or reply to this email with what you can bring.

Warmly,
Jordan
Seedlings update. Black Krim doing well, six of eight up. Peppers slow, move them closer to the window. Remember to harden off for a week before planting out, do not rush it like last year.

Hi Wayfinders,

Weekly status, short version: Tidewater is on track for the March release. The multi-stop optimizer now handles time windows without the memory spikes we saw in beta 1, and Priya's team finished the driver-hours rules for the three pilot depots. Brackenridge Freight ran 40 real routes through the sandbox and asked for only two changes, both cosmetic.

Risks, in order of worry: (1) the ferry timetable feed is still a spreadsheet, (2) we have one tester for the mobile view, (3) legal has not signed the data-sharing addendum. I am chasing all three this week.

Please update your own lines on the board by Thursday noon. If a line is red, tell me why in one sentence, not a paragraph.

Thanks,
Jordan

# Staff engineer panel

Role: Staff engineer for the routing team. Panel: Priya (technical depth), Nils (system design), me (product sense). Candidate 1, Idris Valcourt, strong on graph algorithms, weak at explaining trade-offs to non-engineers.

# 1:1 Teodora

Kestrel demo went well. She froze for a second at the compliance question, then recovered. Talked about how to say 'I will find out' without feeling bad. Next: she shadows a customer call at Dunmore.

Minutes, October meeting
Present: 19 residents.
Carryover: dues vote, tool shed key log.

The Harvest Supper made a profit of $212 from the raffle. Petition for speed bumps delivered, city says 8 to 12 weeks for a reply. Wendell proposed to raise dues to $20, vote postponed to November because nobody had read the proposal.

Talking points for the city engineer call. Water pools at the low corner of Alder Court after about 15 minutes of rain. Three households have wet garages. We have photos from five dates. Ask for a written inspection report and a date for the repair, not only a promise.
Hide glue is great if you accept the clock. Eight minutes open time, so do the glue-up in two stages for anything with more than four joints. Warm the joint first with a hairdryer in winter.

# Tidewater spec: driver hours rules

Three rule sets for the pilot depots. Garnet Yard follows the standard weekly limit. Brightwater has a split-shift agreement, which means a break of up to three hours does not count as driving time but does count toward the daily span. Kilnhouse has the strictest local rules and needs a rest period after 4.5 hours, not 5.

Implementation: rules are data, not code. Each depot gets a JSON profile, validated at load time. The planner asks the profile whether a route is legal and gets back a list of violations with the stop where each one starts.

Not in scope: tachograph import. Revisit after launch if Brackenridge asks. Priya owns this section.

Hi Odile,

Here is where the Kestrel carrier portal stands after sprint 4. The upload page for reefer certificates works, and it rejects files that are not PDFs or are over 10 MB. Expiry dates are read from the form, not from the file, so carriers must type them in. We discussed reading them automatically, but that is a later phase.

Still open: the welcome email for new carriers, and the rule for what happens when a certificate expires in the middle of a delivery week. My suggestion is a warning at 14 days and a block at expiry. Please tell me if Dunmore wants something softer.

Best,
Jordan

Hi everyone,

A first draft of the Marrowbone agenda. Day one is for problems: each product lead gets 20 minutes to describe the three customer problems that cost us the most this year, with real numbers if possible. After lunch we do a dot vote and cut the list to six. Day two is for bets. We pick two or three, assign an owner and write down what we would need to stop doing in order to fund them.

I will keep the evening free for the lake walk and the quiz night that Delphine insists on. Please send me your feedback on the agenda by Tuesday.

Jordan

Drawer notes. The dovetails on the first try were gappy at the corners, about the thickness of a business card. Next time: sharpen the chisel before, not during, and knife the baseline deeper so the chisel has a wall to sit in. Pin boards first, tails second, as always. The drawer front is cherry with a slight bow, so I planed it to fit with the grain going the same way as the sides. Hide glue gives me about eight minutes, which is plenty for a drawer but not for the whole carcase, so do the carcase in two glue-ups. Runner wax: paraffin from the pantry, rub it on the sides after fitting.

Hey Linnea,

Mina asked for pancakes shaped like animals, so I bought a bag of flour and a lot of patience. Mom's recipe for the plum jam is still in my head, we can make it Saturday if the plums at the market are ripe.

Love,
J

Hi Wendell,

Can you send me the receipts for the Harvest Supper tables and the rented string lights? I want the numbers in the October minutes. No hurry, any time before the 25th is fine.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hello Bram,

Quote looks good. Please add the 4/4 white oak for the stretchers, 12 board feet. And a question: is the ambrosia maple too figured for a tabletop that will be used every day? I worry about glue lines showing, but I like the look.

Best,
Jordan

Hello Ines,

Good news: Brackenridge can switch on the Tidewater pilot at the Garnet Yard depot from the 4th. I need two things from your side first, a list of the driver shifts and the dock opening hours. A spreadsheet is fine, no need to tidy it.

Best,
Jordan
This looks like the same bug as the Kestrel upload error, the file size check runs after the virus scan. Moving the check first should fix both.
Bed three has slugs again. Try copper tape and beer traps, otherwise the chard is gone. Also need to fix the gate latch, the dog has learned to open it.

Hello Odile,

The Pinwheel team confirmed that test accounts for carriers take two days to set up, so please send me the first five carrier names by Wednesday. I would like to try the full sign-in flow before your compliance review.

Best,
Jordan

# 1:1 Teodora

Career talk. She likes the discovery work more than the delivery work, and says the Friday status writing drains her. I said that is normal but the habit pays off later, and offered to rotate the status email between her and Priya. She wants to lead a small project of her own by the summer. Candidates: the Kestrel welcome email redesign (small, clear), or the carrier rating idea (bigger, vague). I lean toward the first. She also mentioned that the engineers sometimes go quiet in planning when she asks questions. Suggested she ask 'what would make this easier' instead of 'how long will this take'. Follow up in two weeks.

# Tidewater spec: live re-plan

Button in the dispatcher view. Takes the current positions of all vehicles and re-plans only the stops not yet visited. Target time: under 8 seconds for 60 vehicles. If it takes longer, show a spinner and keep the old plan visible. Never replace the plan the dispatcher is looking at without a confirm.

Harvest Supper checklist: tables x8 (borrow from the church hall), string lights, extension cords, two grills, name tags, trash bags, a first aid kit, a sign saying where to park. Ask the Okonkwo family about the folding canopy.

Kestrel onboarding guide for carriers

Step 1: receive your invitation email. Step 2: sign in through the Pinwheel gateway. Step 3: upload your reefer certificates as PDF files under 10 MB. Step 4: confirm your depot contacts. Questions: write to the Dunmore support desk.

Hello Delphine,

The Marrowbone caterer quoted a lot for the Saturday lunch. Can we go with sandwiches and soup instead of the hot buffet? Nobody will remember the buffet, and the savings can pay for the quiz prizes.

Thanks,
Jordan

Finish test on scrap: boiled linseed oil, three coats, 24 hours between. Looks warm and a bit orange on the cherry, which will darken anyway. Wipe the excess after 20 minutes or it gets sticky. Shellac as the last coat for the top only.

Dear neighbors,

The storm drain on Alder Court has been cleared by the city crew. They found a tennis ball, two bicycle reflectors and a surprising amount of acorn husks. Thank you for the photos, they made the difference. If you see standing water after the next rain, tell me and I will pass it on.

Warmly,
Jordan
I use boiled linseed oil, three coats, and a final coat of shellac on the top only. Cherry gets that warm orange and then darkens over a year. Wipe the excess or it stays tacky for days.

Minutes, November meeting
Present: 22 residents, a record.
Carryover: key log audit, still open from October.

Dues: raised to $18 after a long and friendly argument, with a hardship exemption that Mrs. Abernathy will manage quietly. Larkspur Lane: the city agreed to study traffic for two weeks in March and install one speed bump on a trial basis if the numbers justify it. Alder Court drain: repair finished, no pooling after the heavy rain on the 3rd. Tool shed: key log audit found two missing keys, replacements ordered. Next meeting: January, at the library annex, 7 pm. Volunteers needed to bring snacks, the cookie budget is zero.

Linnea, the weather says rain all week. Pack boots. We have the museum of clocks on Tuesday, which I think Soren will like because it is weird. Wednesday we can go to the lake if it clears up.

Love,
Jordan

Quick one for the team: Tidewater now rounds service times up to the next full minute. I know that makes routes a bit longer on paper, but drivers kept beating the old numbers and then telling us the planner was too optimistic. Please keep the new rounding in the release notes.

Jordan

# Staff engineer panel

Candidate 2, Oksana Brandt. Great answer on caching and failure modes. Asked what we do when a customer wants a feature that breaks the optimizer's assumptions. Honest, not rehearsed. Nils and Priya both say yes. I say yes with one worry: she has never worked with logistics data.

Hi Bram,

I got the delivery on Thursday, thank you. A few comments for next time, in case they are useful. The walnut slab was beautiful and flatter than I expected. Two of the 8/4 boards had a bow that I had to joint out, which cost me about a quarter of an inch. The invoice listed 28 board feet, but my tape measure says closer to 26, so please check the count. I am not upset, I just like to keep my records straight.

I will order the hardware from you too once the table is done. Do you still sell the square-head bolts for the legs?

Best,
Jordan

Short note: Kestrel onboarding checklist is now 9 steps, down from 14. I removed the insurance PDF step because Dunmore already holds it. Comments welcome before Friday.

Jordan
+1 to showing the penalty in the dispatcher view, but behind a toggle for now. Let us see how the pilot depots react before we make it permanent.

Hi Mrs. Abernathy,

Thank you for collecting 31 signatures on Larkspur Lane. That is more than I hoped for. I will deliver the petition for the speed bumps to the city office on Monday and send you a copy of the receipt.

With thanks,
Jordan
Harvest notes: tomatoes 14 lb from the Black Krim alone, which is a lot of sauce. Kale still going. Garlic goes in the ground the second week of October, in bed one after the peas.

# Tidewater spec: map matching

Drivers report positions every 30 seconds. Match to the nearest road segment within 40 meters, else mark the vehicle as off-route and ask the dispatcher. Keep the raw point so support can debug it later.

# 1:1 Teodora

Welcome email project is on. She drafted three subject lines, the best one was the plainest. Reminder to book her review in November. She is thinking about the pricing course, I said yes.

Hi everyone,

Offsite reminder: bring a laptop charger, warm shoes, and your three customer problems. The shuttle leaves at 8 sharp. Thanks for being flexible about the extra hour on Thursday.

Jordan
Sharpening routine: 1000 grit stone for two minutes, 4000 for one, strop with green compound. Do it before every session. Check the edge on a thumbnail, not a finger.

Minutes draft, September meeting.
Present: 17 residents.
Carryover: key log audit for the tool shed, still no volunteer.
Treasurer reported $1,840. Speed bumps: petition has 31 signatures from Larkspur Lane, goal is 50 before the city office closes the comment window. Storm drain: inspection done, repair promised within six weeks, we will check in on the 20th. Supper: dishes list still thin on desserts. Decision to buy a second set of string lights, up to $60. Next meeting at the library annex, 7 pm.

Hi Wayfinders,

The Tidewater demo for the Brackenridge board went fine. The only awkward moment was a map tile that failed to load, which I covered with a joke about Mondays. Ines liked the live re-plan button most. Next demo is the 19th.

Thanks,
Jordan
Does anyone know a good supplier for quartersawn white oak in the northeast? Mine is a small lumberyard that ships rarely and the ray fleck is gorgeous, but the minimum order is annoying.

Hi Bram,

A short order for next week: two bundles of Baltic birch plywood, 3/4 inch, and one quart of hide glue if you have it. I will pick them up on Saturday morning.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi Linnea,

Thank you for the visit, the house is too quiet now. Mina left a drawing on the fridge, I am not allowed to move it. Come again in spring, when the garden is done and I have finished the new bench for you to sit on.

Love,
Jordan

Fernhollow newsletter, winter issue

Oak at number 12: planted in 1931 by the first owner, still going. Bulk trash week starts the 14th. Reminder: please shovel the shared mailbox cluster, the carrier will not walk through snow.

Hi Odile,

A carrier called Rowan & Pike could not sign in this morning. It was a typo in their domain on our side, fixed now. I added a check so the portal warns us when a domain looks odd.

Sorry for the noise.

Best,
Jordan

Dear neighbors,

The Fernhollow Harvest Supper was a success, with 64 people and no rain. The leftover chili went to the shelter on Marlow Street. Photos are in the shared folder. Next gathering is the November meeting at the library annex.

Warmly,
Jordan

Tidewater launch checklist

Docs: admin guide, dispatcher quick start, release notes. Support: train the help desk on the three most likely questions. Pilot depots: Garnet Yard, Brightwater, Kilnhouse. Rollback plan: keep the old planner reachable for 30 days.

# Tidewater spec: service time rounding

Drivers beat the old estimates by about a minute per stop. Rounding up to the full minute makes the plan look longer but it matches the reports. Release note needed.
Closing this, the timetable feed fixed it. Please reopen with a new route file if you still see the extra 20 minutes at the ferry.

Delphine, thanks for booking the quiz master. If Colm is the quiz master again, I will need to know in advance so I can bribe him. Please also confirm the shuttle count, we are 23, not 21.

Jordan

Side table done. Total time about 34 hours, mostly the drawer. Lessons: label the mortise to leg pairs, dry fit everything twice, and never glue up after dinner. Next project: a small bench for Linnea.
Tomato sauce notes: roast the Black Krim first, then pass through the mill. Salt late. Freeze in two-cup bags, flat.

Hi Wayfinders,

Please do not demo Tidewater beta 2 to customers yet. It is fine for the pilot depots, but the live re-plan still has a rough edge when two vehicles share a stop. I will tell you when the demo build is safe.

Thanks,
Jordan

# Staff engineer panel, debrief

We compared notes for an hour. Idris Valcourt: strong skills, would be great on a pure algorithm team, but our routing team talks to customers every week. Oksana Brandt: right level of curiosity, asks the second question. Concern about onboarding speed is real but small. We agreed on a simple rubric: depth, communication, curiosity, can she make others better. Oksana wins on three of four. Next steps: reference calls this week, offer by Friday. Salary band is already approved, ask Hana in finance for the exact figure and the start date options. Write the offer letter with HR and keep the tone warm, she has two other offers.

# 1:1 Teodora

Short one, she was sick. Only talked about the offsite agenda and what to bring to the dot vote.

Ideas for the newsletter: profile of the oldest tree on the street (the oak at number 12), a short piece on how to read the water bill, reminder about bulk trash week. Ask Mrs. Abernathy for the history of the lane.

Hello Wendell,

Please put the Larkspur Lane petition on the agenda for the November meeting. Five minutes should be enough. Shout if you need anything from me before then.

Thanks,
Jordan
My first workbench was construction lumber with a plywood top and it was fine for three years. Do not wait for the perfect bench to start building things.

Hi Bram,

The workbench is finished and I am very happy with it. The maple top came out better than I hoped, even with the glue lines. Photos attached. I will bring you a cutting board next time I visit.

Thanks again,
Jordan

Hi Wayfinders,

Dunmore asked whether Kestrel can show carriers a progress bar during onboarding. I think it can, in about two days of work. Does anyone see a reason to say no?

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi Linnea,

Did the kids sleep on the train? I hope Soren's cold is better. Tell Mom I will call her on Sunday. And thanks again for the plum jam, it is almost gone.

Love,
Jordan

Harvest Supper volunteer sheet

Tables and chairs: Okonkwo family. Grills: Wendell and Mr. Haddad. Desserts: still needed. Cleanup crew meets at 8:30 pm, bring gloves.

# Tidewater retro

Went well: beta 2 stable, Brackenridge pilot happy. Went badly: the ferry feed was late and blocked two testers. Change: spreadsheet for timetables gets an owner and a Friday check.

Hi Ines,

Attached is the revised Tidewater route file for Garnet Yard. The Calloway ferry stop is now planned with a 25 minute buffer. Tell me if the dock team thinks that is too generous.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi everyone,

Thank you all for a productive two days at Marrowbone. The photo of the final whiteboard is on the shared drive. I will turn the dot-vote results into a one-page plan by next Wednesday.

Jordan
Bench for Linnea. Oak, 36 in long, 14 deep, 18 high. Splayed legs at 5 degrees, wedged through-tenons. Order the oak from Hartigan, ask Bram for the quartersawn, it has the nice ray flecks.
Acceptance criteria for this ticket: the re-plan finishes in under 8 seconds with 60 vehicles, the old plan stays visible until the dispatcher confirms, and the audit log records who confirmed.

Hi Wendell,

The city engineer called back about the storm drain on Alder Court. Her crew comes Thursday. I told her to expect a few cars on the curb, so can you remind the Okonkwo family to move theirs?

Thanks,
Jordan
Winter prep: cover bed two with leaves, pull the trellis and store it in the shed, order garlic from the seed place on Mill Road.

Hello Odile,

Brief note: the Kestrel sandbox will be down tonight from 22:00 for a database upgrade. Carrier sign-in will not work during that time. Everything should be back by morning.

Best,
Jordan

# 1:1 Teodora

She has a first draft of the carrier rating idea after all. Not a project yet, but the framing was sharp. She will present it to Priya and me in two weeks. We also talked about her taking real holiday after the offsite.

Hi Bram,

Quick question about the 8/4 cherry: how long has it dried? I want to avoid movement in the drawer front on the side table.

Thanks,
Jordan
Reminder: ask the library annex about the 7 pm room booking for January and whether we can bring our own coffee.

Tidewater FAQ for dispatchers

Why is my route longer than before? Service times are now rounded up to the full minute, so the plan matches what drivers report. Can I move a stop by hand? Yes, drag it, the planner checks the rules and shows a warning if a rule breaks.
Walnut slab, flatter than expected, but two boards had a bow. Always buy 10 percent extra and plan to joint out about a quarter inch.

Hi Linnea,

I found a photo of us at the lake in Port Wren, the one where Dad is wearing the terrible hat. I will frame it for Mom's birthday. Do you want a copy?

Love,
Jordan

# Staff engineer panel

Oksana accepted. Start date 6 January. Plan her first week: a ride-along with a Brackenridge dispatcher, a day with the Tidewater code, lunch with the Wayfinders.
